data.long_meaning: In Islamic and Arabic tradition, Khanam refers to the lady of Paradise, symbolizing the highest level of spiritual attainment and eternal beauty. It is derived from the Arabic root 'khanana' meaning 'to protect' and 'to keep', indicating the nurturing and guardianship of the divine. The name Khanam carries the meaning “Lady of Paradise” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khanam usually hope their child will grow to embody lady of paradise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
